content.user_title: Build Drug Discovery Models with TorchDrug
content.value_statement: Drug discovery teams need clear guidance for selecting molecular datasets, graph models, and evaluation workflows. This skill provides TorchDrug patterns for molecules, proteins, knowledge graphs, generation, and retrosynthesis.
actual_capabilities: Explains TorchDrug graph, molecule, protein, model, and task interfaces.
Recommends datasets, models, split strategies, losses, and metrics for molecular property prediction.
Compares sequence and structure approaches for protein prediction tasks.
Guides biomedical knowledge graph completion and drug repurposing workflows.
Outlines molecular generation and retrosynthesis pipelines with validation steps.
Troubleshoots dimension mismatches, memory limits, data leakage, and invalid molecular outputs.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not run experiments.
Dataset and model availability may differ across TorchDrug versions.
Generated molecules and routes require chemistry validation and expert review.
Model predictions are research outputs, not clinical or safety decisions.

use_cases.title: Screen Molecular Properties
use_cases.description: Select a dataset, graph model, split strategy, and metrics for an ADMET prediction experiment.

use_cases.title: Model Protein Functions
use_cases.description: Compare sequence and structure models for enzyme, stability, localization, or interaction prediction.

use_cases.title: Plan Generative Chemistry Workflows
use_cases.description: Design validated molecular generation or retrosynthesis workflows with constraints, ranking, and expert review.

prompt_templates.title: Understand TorchDrug Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain TorchDrug data structures and task interfaces for a beginner. Show how molecules, proteins, models, and prediction tasks connect.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learning the library before starting an experiment

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Property Prediction Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a TorchDrug workflow for predicting [property] from [dataset]. Include splitting, model choice, task setup, metrics, and leakage checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Designing a molecular property prediction experiment

prompt_templates.title: Compare Protein Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ESM, GearNet, and SchNet for [protein task]. Consider available sequence data, structures, compute limits, pre-training, and evaluation metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Selecting a protein architecture for a research project

prompt_templates.title: Design a Validated Discovery Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an end-to-end TorchDrug pipeline for [goal]. Cover data curation, architecture, training, uncertainty, chemistry validation, ranking, and expert review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning an advanced molecular generation or retrosynthesis workflow

output_examples.input: Choose a workflow for predicting blood-brain barrier penetration.
output: Use BBBP with a scaffold split to measure structural generalization.
Start with GIN and binary property prediction.
Report AUROC and AUPRC, then inspect scaffold-specific errors.

output_examples.input: Compare ESM and GearNet for enzyme function prediction.
output_examples.output: ESM suits sequence-only data and benefits from pre-training. GearNet uses structural relationships and is stronger when reliable three-dimensional structures are available.

output_examples.input: Create a validation plan for generated molecules.
output: Check chemical validity, uniqueness, novelty, and internal diversity.
Filter for drug-likeness, synthetic accessibility, and unwanted substructures.
Require medicinal chemistry review before synthesis or biological testing.

best_practices: State the task, data modality, prediction target, and available compute before selecting a model.
Use scaffold or structure-aware splits when random splits could inflate performance.
Validate generated molecules and synthesis routes with chemistry tools and domain experts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat predicted activity as experimental or clinical evidence.
Do not use random splits when scaffold generalization is the real objective.
Do not optimize one score while ignoring validity, selectivity, and synthesizability.

faq.question: Does this skill execute TorchDrug experiments?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, implementation guidance, examples, and troubleshooting for experiments run in your environment.

faq.question: Which scientific tasks are covered?
faq.answer: It covers molecular properties, protein modeling, knowledge graphs, molecular generation, retrosynthesis, and graph neural network selection.

faq.question: Can it recommend datasets and models?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps common tasks to TorchDrug datasets, architectures, losses, metrics, and splitting strategies.

faq.question: Does it guarantee chemically valid results?
faq.answer: No. Generated structures and routes require RDKit checks, feasibility filtering, and expert chemistry review.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: Small examples may run on a CPU, but protein models and large graph workloads often require substantial memory and GPU compute.

faq.question: Can predictions support clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. TorchDrug predictions require experimental validation and must not replace clinical, toxicological, or regulatory assessment.
